R001.fact: For every natural m, m! is a positive integer and its image in C is nonzero. A finite product of positive integers likewise has nonzero image in C, including the empty product 1. Hence all factorial divisions and cancellations in D003,D004,D009 and S003,S007 are legitimate.

grounds.reason: V is a complex vector space, so the scalar field for these operations is C.
The divided-power index r is natural.
The divided-power index r is natural.
The basis-family index i is natural and finite.
For 1<=r<=i<=ell, both r and ell-r+1 are positive integers.
All factorial arguments are natural, with ell-i>=0 and the stated endpoint guards.

R001.justification: Induction using 0!=1 and (m+1)!=(m+1)m! gives positivity. The usual integer embedding into C is injective (C has characteristic zero), so positive integers remain nonzero. The field has no zero divisors, and the inverse of a nonzero scalar allows the displayed divisions and cancellations.

R002.fact: For every natural r, r! is a positive natural integer, hence its images in Z and C are nonzero. Thus (r!:C)(r!:C)^(-1)=1, and multiplication by a product of factorials can be cancelled in Z or C.

grounds.reason: D003 defines X_r using the complex inverse of r! for natural r.
D004 defines Y_r with the same natural factorial denominator.

R002.justification: The empty factorial product is 1; every factor of any nonempty factorial is a positive integer. Their finite product is positive. The standard embeddings Z→C and N→Z preserve these nonzero integers, and cancellation follows in the integral domain Z and field C.

R002.fact: For a complex basis (e_k) indexed by Fin(n), prescribing images w_k in V defines a unique complex-linear endomorphism T of V with T(e_k)=w_k. In particular the prescription w_k=e_i if k=j and 0 otherwise defines E_ij.

grounds.reason: N001 states that (e_k) indexed by Fin(n) is a complex basis of V.
The prescribed images lie in V and the indices i,j,k lie in Fin(n).

R002.justification: Every vector has a unique finite basis expansion sum_k a_k e_k. Set T(sum_k a_k e_k)=sum_k a_k w_k. Uniqueness of coordinates makes this well-defined; addition and scalar multiplication of coordinates prove complex linearity. The same expansion proves uniqueness.

R002.fact: For a Z-submodule M of V with injective inclusion iota, restrictions of ambient linear operators preserving M intertwine with iota. Restriction respects composition, integer scalar multiples, finite sums and identity. Hence an ambient equality built from these operations implies the corresponding equality in End_Z(M).

grounds.reason: M is the stated Z-submodule and is stable under the divided-power-generated U_Z.
S001 establishes preservation by X_r,Y_r and the injective inclusion.
D016 defines Q_M as the product of the appropriate restrictions.
D017 defines A_ij as a product of those restrictions.
F005 establishes the ambient product and finite diagonal-sum identities with integer coefficients.

R002.justification: For m in M, applying inclusion to a restricted operator gives the ambient operator applied to iota(m). Repeated substitution proves the same statement for compositions, sums and integer multiples, using additivity of inclusion. After applying an ambient identity at iota(m), injectivity gives the desired equality at m. Pointwise equality gives equality of endomorphisms; no preservation by the unscaled coordinate operators is required.

R003.fact: Every field L satisfies the strong rank condition: an injective L-linear map L^r to L^s for finite natural r,s implies r<=s. In particular this holds for C in S001 and K in S002.

grounds.reason: V is a vector space over the standard field C; M009 is applied over C.
K is explicitly a field; M005 is applied over K.

R003.justification: The images of the r standard basis vectors under an injective map are linearly independent in L^s. Gaussian elimination of the s-by-r matrix uses field division by nonzero pivots and gives at most s pivot columns. Independence requires all r columns to be pivot columns, so r<=s. This verifies the strong rank premises without assuming any target dimension formula.

R003.fact: A finite-dimensional vector space is finitely generated as a module over its field. A finite set I of cardinality n admits a bijection Fin(n) to I.

grounds.reason: lambda is nonnegative, identifying it with ell.
The ordinary complex dimension of V is the finite integer lambda+1.
M008 makes I finite and M009 identifies its natural cardinality with n before the bijection is chosen.

R003.justification: Finite dimension means a finite basis exists, and that basis is a finite spanning set, which is exactly finite generation. A finite set of cardinality n can be enumerated by its n distinct elements, giving the stated bijection. Thus the chosen beta depends on an established finite cardinality, not on an unsupported choice of lattice basis.

R003.fact: If b:I to M is an R-basis and beta:J to I is a bijection, then j maps to b(beta(j)) is an R-basis. Over a nonzero field every vector of a basis is nonzero.

grounds.reason: H007 provides bZ as an integer basis with the corresponding complex basis.
F001 provides the finite-cardinality bijection used for beta.
qBasis is the canonical K-basis supplied by base change, indexed by Fin(n), and n=ell+1 is positive.

R003.justification: Under a bijection, finite coordinate families are reindexed bijectively; spanning expansions and uniqueness of coefficients are preserved. If a basis vector were zero, the finite coefficient family with coefficient 1 at its index and 0 elsewhere would represent zero, contradicting uniqueness against the all-zero family. K is a field, so 1 differs from 0.

R003.fact: For an algebraic tensor product over Z, a biadditive Z-balanced rule into an abelian group extends uniquely to an additive map. Two additive maps agreeing on every pure tensor agree everywhere. For a fixed scalar, equality expressing K-linearity can likewise be checked on pure tensors when both sides are additive.

grounds.reason: The tensor products are algebraic, generated additively by pure tensors with additivity and Z-balancing relations.
U uses the corresponding first-factor K-action.
The formula for F(f) is biadditive and balanced because f is Z-linear.

R003.justification: Present the tensor product as the free abelian group on pairs modulo the biadditivity and balancing relations. Any rule satisfying those relations descends to the quotient. Every element is a finite integer combination of generators; integer coefficients can be absorbed into a tensor factor. Additivity therefore extends equality from pure tensors to all elements. Multiplication by a fixed K scalar is additive, so equality of the two additive maps in a scalar-compatibility identity can also be tested on generators. The later applications must, and do, check their particular formulas; the background fact itself uses only the supplied algebraic tensor-product definitions.

R003.fact: If S:A to B is a linear isomorphism, T:A to A and Q:B to B are linear, and ST=QS, then W maps to S(W) is a bijection between T-invariant subspaces of A and Q-invariant subspaces of B, with inverse Z maps to S_inv(Z). It sends zero and whole spaces to zero and whole spaces.

grounds.reason: F004 gives the K-linear isomorphism S and its inverse.
F(f) is a K-linear operator on U.
ind(f) is a K-linear operator on V_K.
For arbitrary f0, the displayed pure-tensor calculation proves S ind(f0)=F(f0) S everywhere.

R003.justification: The image of a subspace under a linear map is a subspace. If T(W) is contained in W, then Q(S(W))=S(T(W)) is contained in S(W). From ST=QS and the inverse identities one obtains T S_inv=S_inv Q, proving the converse for inverse images. The mutually inverse maps S and S_inv make these subspace assignments inverse bijections. Linearity sends zero to zero and surjectivity sends A onto B.

R004.fact: For the supplied unital ring homomorphism F:End_Z(M)→End_K(U), every integer t and f∈End_Z(M) satisfy F(t·f)=red(t)·F(f). For K-linear endomorphisms P,Q and scalars a,b∈K, (a·P)(b·Q)=(ab)·(PQ).

grounds.reason: F is explicitly a unital ring homomorphism with codomain End_K(U).
red is the canonical integer map into K.

R004.justification: For nonnegative t, additivity gives F(t·f)=t·F(f) by finite induction; preservation of negation extends this to integers. In End_K(U), this repeated integer addition equals multiplication by red(t), as seen on each vector. Also P(bQ(u))=bP(Q(u)) by K-linearity, so evaluation gives (aP)(bQ)(u)=ab(PQ)(u). These facts justify the scalar transfers and rearrangements used in S002 and again in S003.

R004.fact: For a K-linear subspace W of U, if P preserves W then P^s preserves W for every natural s. If P and Q preserve W, then PQ preserves W, and aP preserves W for every a∈K.

grounds.reason: W is an arbitrary K-linear subspace of U.
L2 assumes stability under F(x_M) and F(y_M); F003 supplies scalar-power formulas before they are used.
Stability means that each vector of W is mapped into W.
The divided-power formulas hold for all indices at most ell.

R004.justification: The identity preserves W. Inductively, P^(s+1)(w)=P(P^s(w)) lies in W. Similarly, PQ(w) lies in W by applying Q and then P, and aP(w) lies in W by closure of a K-subspace under scalar multiplication. Applying these facts to F003 and to the four factors displayed in S004 verifies precisely the stated stability step.

R005.fact: For a vector u≠0 in a vector space over a field k, a·u=0 implies a=0. For a finite index type I, a family b:I→U is linearly independent precisely when every relation ∑_{i∈I} a_i·b_i=0 has all a_i=0.

grounds.reason: The current k0 is a field, U0 is a k0-vector space, and the index type is Fin(n0).
F003 proves u0≠0.
The displayed operator calculation derives acoef_kidx·u0=0 for arbitrary coefficients satisfying L4 and arbitrary kidx.

R005.justification: If a≠0, multiplication of a·u=0 by a^{-1} gives u=0, a contradiction. Linear independence means that the kernel of the map taking a finitely supported coefficient family to its linear combination is zero. On finite I every coefficient family is finitely supported and this map is the displayed finite sum. Thus the coefficient extraction in S005 proves the required independence.

R005.fact: If every vector b_i of a family belongs to a k-linear subspace W≤U, then span_k(range b)⊆W. Consequently, if that span equals U, then W=U.

grounds.reason: W0 is a k0-linear subspace of U0.
F003 places every uFamily_i in W0.
The verified application of M001 gives span_k0(range uFamily)=U0.

R005.justification: A linear subspace contains zero and is closed under scalar multiplication and addition, so it contains every finite linear combination of the family. These combinations constitute its span. The span equality therefore gives U0⊆W0, while W0⊆U0 holds by its subspace type.

R006.fact: For the free rank-three Chevalley Lie algebra L_Z of D026 and its scalar extension L_K of D027, K-linear operators A,B,H satisfying [H,A]=2A, [H,B]=-2B and [A,B]=H define a Lie action by sending the three formal generators to A,B,H and extending K-linearly. A K-linear subspace is invariant under this action exactly when it is invariant under A,B,H. This holds in every characteristic.

grounds.reason: L_Z is free on the three formal generators and its bracket is alternating and Z-bilinear with the displayed generator relations.
L_K is the scalar extension with the bracket and proposed action extended K-linearly.
H005 gives the corresponding three commutators on V.
N002 gives the intertwining of the integral restrictions with x,y,h through inclusion.
N003 gives the ring homomorphism F and the K-linear isomorphism S intertwining F with ind.

R006.justification: The restriction relations in S001 follow pointwise through the injective inclusion. A unital ring homomorphism preserves differences, products and integer multiples, so F preserves those relations; conjugating by S preserves them for A=ind(x_M), B=ind(y_M), H=ind(h_M). The three scalar-extended formal generators span L_K. Expand both the Lie bracket and the endomorphism commutator bilinearly: their values agree on each pair of generators by the three displayed relations, their reversed relations and the zero diagonal commutators. Hence they agree on all elements. This uses no division, including in characteristic 2. For invariance, each action is a K-linear combination of A,B,H, so closure of the subspace under addition and scalar multiplication gives the forward implication; the reverse implication follows by selecting the generators.

argument.text: H003 gives lambda≥0, hence lambda=(ell:Z) by the definition of Int.toNat, and ell<p. Thus n=ell+1 and H004 gives dim_C V=n. H006 becomes v≠0, xv=0, hv=ell·v. No property of reduction into K is used here.

argument.text: H005 gives hy=yh−2y and xy=yx+h. Prove h y^i v=(ell−2i)y^i v for every i≥0 by induction: the base is F001; for the step fix t and temporarily assume L1: h y^t v=(ell−2t)y^t v. Then h y^(t+1)v=(yh−2y)y^t v=(ell−2t−2)y^(t+1)v. Discharge L1 to the induction step. For the second identity the base is xyv=yxv+hv=ell v. In the step t≥1, assume L2: xy^t v=t(ell−t+1)y^(t−1)v. Then xy^(t+1)v=y(xy^t v)+hy^t v=[t(ell−t+1)+(ell−2t)]y^t v=(t+1)(ell−t)y^t v. Discharge L2; induction gives xy^i v=i(ell−i+1)y^(i−1)v for every i≥1. These identities do not assume termination.

produces.statement: For every i≥0, hy^i v=(ell−2i)y^i v; for every i≥1, xy^i v=i(ell−i+1)y^(i−1)v.

argument.text: For each 0≤i≤ell, repeated use of F002 gives x^i y^i v=[∏_{r=1}^i r(ell−r+1)]v. For i>0 all displayed factors are positive integers; for i=0 the product is 1. In C they are nonzero, so v≠0 forces y^i v≠0. Since i!≠0, e_i≠0. F002 also gives he_i=(ell−2i)e_i. The eigenvalues are pairwise distinct: ell−2i=ell−2j in C implies 2(i−j)=0 and hence i=j in characteristic zero.

produces.statement: For every ii∈Fin(n), e_ii≠0 and he_ii=(ell−2ii)e_ii; the eigenvalue family (ell−2ii)_{ii∈Fin(n)} is pairwise distinct in C.

argument.text: Take arbitrary coefficients zeta and temporarily assume L3: ∑_i zeta_i e_i=0. Fix j∈Fin(n) and apply ∏_{k≠j}(h−(ell−2k)Id). The factors commute because each is a polynomial in h. Every term of index i≠j is killed by its factor k=i; the surviving term is zeta_j[∏_{k≠j}((ell−2j)−(ell−2k))]e_j=0. By F003 the product and e_j are nonzero, including the empty product. Thus zeta_j=0. This holds for every j. Discharging L3 proves complex linear independence of e.

produces.statement: The family e:Fin(n)→V is C-linearly independent.

argument.text: Apply M001 with division ring C, vector space V, index set Fin(n), and family e. Fin(n) has n elements, V is finite-dimensional of dimension n by F001, and F004 supplies independence. The span is V. Together with independence this makes e a basis.

produces.statement: The family e:Fin(n)→V is a complex basis of V.

argument.text: Put zvec=y^(ell+1)v and alpha_i its e-basis coordinates. M006 with this basis expands zvec=∑_i alpha_i e_i. F002 gives h zvec=(−ell−2)zvec, and applying h−(−ell−2)Id to this expansion gives ∑_i alpha_i[2(ell+1−i)]e_i=0. For every i≤ell the bracketed integer is positive, hence nonzero in C. Independence F004 forces every alpha_i=0, so zvec=0. Applying further powers of y gives y^s v=0 for all s≥ell+1.

produces.statement: y^(ell+1)v=0, and y^s v=0 for every natural s≥ell+1.

argument.text: Divide the recurrences F002 by i!, using (i+1)!=(i+1)i!, and combine F006 at the top endpoint. This gives xe_0=0, xe_i=(ell−i+1)e_(i−1) for i≥1, ye_i=(i+1)e_(i+1) for i<ell, ye_ell=0 and he_i=(ell−2i)e_i. For r≤i, iteration of x yields ∏_{s=1}^r(ell−i+s) on e_(i−r). After division by r!, M004 at (n0,j0)=(ell−i+r,r), and cancellation of (ell−i)!≠0 in C, gives choose(ell−i+r,r). If r>i the string reaches e_0 and is killed. For i+r≤ell, iteration of y yields (i+r)!/i! on e_(i+r); division by r!, using M004 at (i+r,r), gives choose(i+r,r). If i+r>ell the string reaches e_ell and is killed by y. Thus both zero cases and r=0 are included. These formulas together with F001,F005,F006 prove the full coordinate and termination statement.

argument.text: By H007 every X_r,Y_r preserves M, so its restriction is a Z-linear endomorphism. Inclusion M→V is injective because M is a submodule. The original complex identities r!X_r=x^r and r!Y_r=y^r therefore restrict to r!X_M(r)=x_M^r and r!Y_M(r)=y_M^r for every r≥0. These are identities using integer multiples of operators, with no division in M. By H005, h=xy−yx, so h preserves M and restricts to h_M=x_M y_M−y_M x_M. The inclusions intertwine x_M,y_M,h_M with x,y,h.

produces.statement: For every natural r, r!X_M(r)=x_M^r and r!Y_M(r)=y_M^r; inclusion M→V is injective and intertwines x_M,y_M,h_M with x,y,h.

argument.text: N001 supplies the complex basis e. Define its coordinate endomorphisms E_ij by E_ij e_k=delta_(j,k)e_i. They exist by linear extension on a basis. To record how operator equalities will be checked, fix arbitrary complex endomorphisms fop,gop and temporarily assume L1 that they agree on each e_i. M007, with scalar homomorphism Id_C, yields fop=gop. Discharging L1 and quantifying these maps gives: any two complex-linear endomorphisms agreeing on every e_i are equal.

produces.statement: For any two complex-linear endomorphisms of V, agreement on every e_i implies equality.

argument.text: Put Q_C=Y_ell X_ell. The N001 divided-power formulas show X_ell kills e_k for k<ell and sends e_ell to e_0, while Y_ell e_0=e_ell. Thus Q_C=E_(ell,ell), by F002. They also give X_(ell−i)e_ell=e_i (its binomial coefficient is choose(ell−i,ell−i)=1), so X_(ell−i)Q_C=E_(i,ell) for every i. All formulas include ell=0.

produces.statement: Q_C=E_(ell,ell) and, for every ii∈Fin(n), X_(ell−ii)Q_C=E_(ii,ell).

argument.text: Put A_C_ij=X_(ell−i)Q_C Y_(ell−j). On e_k, if k<j the vector Y_(ell−j)e_k has index below ell and is killed by Q_C; if k>j it goes past the top index and is already zero. For k=j it is choose(ell,ell−j)e_ell. M004 at (ell,j) and (ell,ell−j) gives choose(ell,j) j!(ell−j)!=ell!=choose(ell,ell−j)(ell−j)!j!. Cancel the nonzero integer factorial product to obtain choose(ell,ell−j)=choose(ell,j)=c_j. Hence Q_C Y_(ell−j)=c_j E_(ell,j), and F003 gives A_C_ij=c_j E_ij. In each instance equality on every basis vector is promoted to equality of endomorphisms by F002.

produces.statement: For every ii,jj∈Fin(n), Q_C Y_(ell−jj)=c(jj) E(ell,jj) and A_C(ii,jj)=c(jj) E(ii,jj).

argument.text: On every basis vector, E_ij E_kl equals E_il if j=k and 0 otherwise; F002 proves the operator identity. By F004, A_C_ij A_C_kl=c_j A_C_il if j=k (both sides are c_j c_l E_il), and 0 otherwise. By definition d_j c_j=Dprod, also for the singleton index set. Acting on e_k gives (∑_j d_j A_C_jj)e_k=Dprod e_k. F002 therefore gives ∑_j d_j A_C_jj=Dprod Id_V.

produces.statement: For all ii,jj,kk,ll∈Fin(n), A_C(ii,jj) A_C(kk,ll)=c(jj) A_C(ii,ll) when jj=kk, and 0 otherwise. Also, for every jj∈Fin(n), d(jj)c(jj)=Dprod, and the finite diagonal sum ∑_{q∈Fin(n)} d(q) A_C(q,q)=Dprod Id_V.

argument.text: The products defining Q_M,A_ij are restrictions of Q_C,A_C_ij, since all their divided-power factors preserve M. Thus all coefficients and operators in F005 preserve M, and composition with the injective inclusion M→V transfers each identity to End_Z(M): A_ij A_kl=c_j A_il for j=k and 0 otherwise, and ∑_j d_j A_jj=Dprod Id_M. Along with d_j c_j=Dprod and F001 this proves the full integral-operator statement. Only c_j E_ij is asserted to preserve M over Z.

Since n=ell+1>0, the index 0 exists. qBasis_0≠0: its own basis coordinate at 0 is 1≠0 in K. Thus U≠0.

argument.text: The K,M,F names in E001's verbatim source statement are source-bound (their ledger aliases are k0,M0,G0). Apply E001 with its source field/module instantiated by the problem K,M, giving a unital ring homomorphism G with G(f)(a⊗m)=a⊗f(m). This is the same pure-tensor formula as D020 F. For each f, both G(f) and F(f) are additive maps, and every tensor is a finite sum of pure tensors, so they agree everywhere. Thus F=G as functions and F itself preserves 1, multiplication, 0 and addition. In particular finite sums, powers, negative operators and integer multiples are preserved. This identifies the prepared adapter with the actual operators used here.

produces.statement: F is a unital ring homomorphism End_Z(M)→End_K(U), with F(f)(a⊗m)=a⊗f(m) for every f,a,m.

argument.text: The formulas defining S,S_inv are additive in each input and Z-balanced: for an integer t, the tensor relation a⊗(t m)=(t a)⊗m verifies that moving t between the inputs gives the same value, and the reversed tensor relation verifies this for S_inv. Thus the additive tensor maps are well-defined. For any b,a∈K and m∈M, S(b·(m⊗a))=S(m⊗ba)=ba⊗m=b·S(m⊗a); the same calculation proves K-linearity of S_inv. Their composites fix every pure tensor and hence every finite sum of pure tensors. They are therefore mutual inverses. From F002, U≠0; the isomorphism S then gives V_K≠0.

produces.statement: S:V_K→U is a K-linear isomorphism with inverse S_inv, and V_K≠0.

argument.text: Fix f0 and a pure tensor m0⊗a0. By the defining formulas, S(ind(f0)(m0⊗a0))=S(f0(m0)⊗a0)=a0⊗f0(m0)=F(f0)(S(m0⊗a0)). Equality extends to every tensor by additivity. Thus S ind(f0)=F(f0) S for every f0. If a subspace is invariant under ind(f0), its image under S is invariant under F(f0); conversely use S_inv. The inverse identities also send zero and whole spaces to zero and whole spaces. With F002,F003,F004 this proves the full scalar-extension, dimension and intertwining statement.

argument.text: H003 gives lambda=(ell:Z) and ell<p. Since p is prime and char K=p (H001,H002), M003 at r0=ell gives that red(ell!) is a unit, hence nonzero in the field K. For j∈Fin(n), M004 at (ell,j) gives c_j j!(ell−j)!=ell!. After applying red this is red(c_j) red(j!) red((ell−j)!)=red(ell!)≠0. No factor of a nonzero product in a field can be zero, so red(c_j)≠0 for every j. The finite product red(Dprod)=∏_j red(c_j) is nonzero.

produces.statement: For every jj∈Fin(n), red(c(jj))≠0; also red(Dprod)≠0.

argument.text: Use the ring-homomorphism laws of F from N003 on N002. Integer multiples of an endomorphism become scalar multiples by their image in K: repeated addition and negation commute with F. Scalars commute with K-linear maps. When j≠k, the integer multiplication identity gives T_ij T_k,lidx=0. When j=k it gives T_ij T_j,lidx=red(c_j)^(-1)red(c_lidx)^(-1)F(c_j A_i,lidx)=red(c_lidx)^(-1)F(A_i,lidx)=T_i,lidx. Cancellation uses F001. The sum identity becomes ∑_j red(d_j)F(A_jj)=red(Dprod)Id_U. From d_j c_j=Dprod and F001, red(d_j)=red(Dprod)red(c_j)^(-1); divide the sum identity by the nonzero red(Dprod) to get ∑_j T_jj=Id_U. These are endomorphism identities on U; no reduction of the characteristic-zero e-basis has been presumed.

produces.statement: For all aidx,bidx,cidx,didx∈Fin(n), T_aidx,bidx T_cidx,didx equals T_aidx,didx when bidx=cidx and 0 otherwise, and ∑_j T_jj=Id_U.

argument.text: Fix arbitrary r and temporarily assume L1: r≤ell. Then r<p. M003 gives red(r!) a unit, hence nonzero. N002 gives r! X_M(r)=x_M^r and r! Y_M(r)=y_M^r; N003 lets us apply F, preserving powers and integer multiples. Therefore F(X_M(r))=red(r!)^(-1)F(x_M)^r and F(Y_M(r))=red(r!)^(-1)F(y_M)^r. Discharge L1 and quantify r. The proof only inverts factorials with indices at most ell<p.

produces.statement: For every natural s≤ell, red(s!)≠0, F(X_M(s))=red(s!)^(-1)F(x_M)^s, and F(Y_M(s))=red(s!)^(-1)F(y_M)^s.

argument.text: Let W be any K-linear subspace of U and temporarily assume L2: W is invariant under F(x_M),F(y_M). By induction it is invariant under every power of each operator, with the identity as the base. Linearity of W and F003 give invariance under F(X_M(r)),F(Y_M(r)) for all r≤ell. The factors in A_ij=X_M(ell−i)Y_M(ell)X_M(ell)Y_M(ell−j) all have indices between 0 and ell, so their F-images preserve W by composition and the ring-homomorphism laws. Finally multiplication by red(c_j)^(-1) preserves W because W is K-linear. Thus every T_ij preserves W. Discharge L2 and universally quantify W. Along with F001,F002 this proves the full reduced matrix-unit and stability statement; Lie invariance has never been used to infer stability of divided powers of index at or above p.

argument.text: H007 and N002 identify x_M,y_M,h_M with the integral restrictions of the stipulated x,y,h. Their integer Chevalley relations follow from H005 by applying the injective inclusion M→V: [h_M,x_M]=2x_M, [h_M,y_M]=−2y_M and [x_M,y_M]=h_M. By N003, scalar extension F preserves these identities, and S intertwines F with each induced operator ind on V_K. Thus the original induced x,y,h actions are exactly ind(x_M),ind(y_M),ind(h_M), with the stipulated Chevalley relations after tensoring over Z. This is valid in characteristic 2 as well: the L_K=L_Z⊗_Z K action is the K-linear extension of the integral action of the three formal Chevalley generators. Invariance under the three generators is equivalent to invariance under every K-linear combination of them. N003 already gives V_K≠0.

Let W be any K-linear subspace of V_K, and assume L1: W is invariant under the induced x,y,h operators. Put Zsub=S(W). By N003 it is a K-linear subspace of U; the intertwining formulas and L1 make it invariant under F(x_M),F(y_M). N004 therefore makes it invariant under all T_ij and supplies the multiplication and diagonal-sum relations. N003 gives dim_K U=n=ell+1>0. Apply N005 at field K, size n, space U, family T and subspace Zsub: Zsub={0} or Zsub=U. Apply S_inv, using the inverse identities in N003, to obtain W={0} or W=V_K. Discharge L1 and quantify W. Together with nonzeroness from N003 this proves P.

For the endpoints, H003 gives ell<p, H001 gives p prime, and H002 gives char K=p. If lambda=0 then ell=0,n=1, X_0=Y_0=Id, c_0=Dprod=d_0=1, and all the same formulas apply. If p=2 then ell∈{0,1}; every factorial inverted in the stability argument has index at most ell<2. The e-basis in N001 lives in V over C; none of the reduced matrix-unit premises used in S002 requires distinct h-eigenvalues in K. No step imposed algebraic closure of K or a minimal-lattice condition. Thus the conclusion covers the complete original parameter range.

value.definition: L_Z is the free abelian group on the three abstract Chevalley generators, denoted x,y,h in the original problem, with Z-bilinear alternating bracket [h,x]=2x, [h,y]=−2y, [x,y]=h. In formulas for the action, the parameter endomorphisms x,y,h are the respective images of these generators; the integral Lie algebra is not defined as their possibly nonfaithful image in End_C(V).

L_K=L(K)=L_Z⊗_Z K=(Zx+Zy+Zh)⊗_Z K in the original Chevalley notation, with the bracket extended K-bilinearly from the integral bracket. The action on V_K assigns the formal generators the operators ind(x_M),ind(y_M),ind(h_M) and extends K-linearly. Its bracket-preserving property is proved separately. This definition includes characteristic 2.

49: /-- The rank of a module as a natural number.
50: 
51: For a finite-dimensional vector space `V` over a field `k`, `Module.finrank k V` is equal to
52: the dimension of `V` over `k`.
53: 
54: For a general module `M` over a ring `R`, `Module.finrank R M` is defined to be the supremum of the
55: cardinalities of the `R`-linearly independent subsets of `M`, if this supremum is finite. It is
56: defined by convention to be `0` if this supremum is infinite. See `Module.rank` for a
57: cardinal-valued version where infinite rank modules have rank an infinite cardinal.
58: 
59: Note that if `R` is not a field then there can exist modules `M` with `¬(Module.Finite R M)` but
60: `finrank R M ≠ 0`. For example `ℚ` has `finrank` equal to `1` over `ℤ`, because the nonempty
61: `ℤ`-linearly independent subsets of `ℚ` are precisely the nonzero singletons. -/

representations_and_conversion_obligatio.notes: Verified the correspondence claims against definitions and pinned Mathlib, not just elaboration. Module.Basis stores a linear equivalence to finitely supported coordinates, so H007 asserts actual spanning and independence over Z and C. FiniteDimensional is Module.Finite; explicit finite-dimensional clauses prevent finrank's infinite-rank-to-zero convention from weakening dimension assertions. Fin(ell+1) means 0 through ell; guards make natural subtractions valid, while all h eigenvalues use complex subtraction. Module.End multiplication is rightmost-first composition. The definitions of dividedPower,e,c,d,Dprod,AC,A,hM,T agree with their source objects and scalar fields; nsmul on integral endomorphisms is repeated addition, not division. In the pinned library baseChange acts by a⊗m↦a⊗f(m), and its endomorphism homomorphism preserves the ring operations. Tensor commutation exchanges the factors with the stated inverse. AddEquiv.module preserves the original additive group and pulls scalar action back through that exchange; consequently VK's action is on the second factor. T008 explicitly requires that pure-tensor scalar rule, both swap formulas, ind(f)(m⊗a)=f(m)⊗a, intertwining, the iff for invariant subspaces, inverse image-map identities, bottom/top transport and nonzeroness. These are faithful worker obligations, not assumed equivalences. T004/T006 separately identify hM with the restriction of source h. T012 checks all three integral and reduced Chevalley relations and both directions of invariance under their linear span; this is the action of the source's formal rank-three Chevalley algebra, including characteristic 2 and the possibly nonfaithful lambda=0 action, not a replacement by its image. Thus the complete target is the source assertion on M⊗Z K, with both directions of every representation crossing accounted for.
